title: Telemetry Concierge and Probabilistic Hypothesis Harness
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: On-call responders frequently need a compact, prioritized snapshot of telemetry together with likely failure hypotheses rather than raw logs. This PR adds a lightweight 'Telemetry Concierge' service that prepares a deterministic, bounded-size package of prioritized metrics/traces/log snippets and pairs it with a probabilistic hypothesis harness that ranks candidate root causes and runbook suggestions. Goals: (1) reduce cognitive load for first responders, (2) enable fast canaryable rollout (opt-in per service/rotation), (3) keep sampling and storage minimal to avoid SLO regressions and cost spikes. Key features: - Telemetry Concierge engine: collects stable, privacy-aware snapshot containing top-N anomalies, delta histograms for critical metrics, representative traces (sampled by anomaly window), and a small context index. Snapshots are versioned and can be requested via CLI/webhook. - Probabilistic Hypothesis Harness: a lightweight scorer that consumes the snapshot and uses feature-weight heuristics + historical hit-rates to produce a ranked list of 3–5 hypotheses, each anchored to evidence snippets and suggested next probes. - Shift-aware deferred sampler: when on-call is busy, the concierge can schedule low-impact deferred sampling (long-tail heap dumps, low-frequency trace captures) that are stored encrypted and linked to the snapshot. - Runbook curator integration: for top hypotheses, we surface runbook fragments with confidence bands and a recommended quick-check sequence. - Safety and opt-in: sampling is opt-in per-service and respects scrubbing and retention policies. Feature flags allow rollout, and sampling budgets are enforced at the agent and server. Implementation notes: Service scoped inside slo-toolkit as pkg/concierge with agent shim for instrumentation; snapshot format is stable JSON schema v1 (compact, delta-encoded), storage by default keeps last 30 snapshots per service with TTLs configurable. Rollout plan: Stage 1 (beta): internal teams only, flag off for customer accounts. Stage 2: opt-in per-customer. Stage 3: broader default with aggressive budget enforcement. Checklist: - [x] Core engine + scorer implemented - [x] CLI and webhook endpoints added - [x] Basic unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: oncall quickstart and runbook mapping - [x] Feature flags + budgets wired - [x] Security review notes added in PR comments - [x] Perf validation on staging (latency < 3ms added on snapshot path) Backwards compatibility: Snapshot schema v1 additive; agents continue to function when concierge endpoint is disabled. Performance: measured under staging workloads; typical snapshot creation adds ~2–4ms median CPU work on agents, server indexing uses bounded queues. Operational concerns: Ensure sampling budgets are tuned for high-cardinality services; recommend default budget = 5 snapshots/hour/service for first rollout.
